answer: Physical Presence Ledger: each identity is bound to a kernel-level hardware key that signs a fresh, locally measured device-fingerprint bundle every epoch, and registration requires one continuous hardware attestation session witnessed by a nearby node. Cloned software instances share no unique silicon, so they cannot produce distinct signatures. The vine of trust grows only from verified sessions, creating a haven from replay. Attackers must buy and physically host one distinct device per identity, making each fake identity cost real hardware and ongoing power, not just compute.
